note: Outside the stated ICP on three of five criteria, and on the two that matter commercially. He is a retired police officer working per-diem road details roughly once a week to supplement his pension — not a business owner, physician or equivalent — so 'successful' fails on the criterion as written even though thirty-two years of service and a wellness-coordinator role are creditable by any other measure. Income fails explicitly and in his own words: 'I'm on a fixed income', existing debts to clear, and 'I can't justify spending that much money on myself.' Neglected health fails in the opposite direction from most misses in this corpus — he trains three to five times a week, eats clean, drinks no soda, holds personal training certifications and ran bootcamp classes for his department. Health is the area he has attended to most. He does match good-to-great, wanting to sharpen an already committed practice, and he is emphatically not deconditioned or gym-averse. Two findings worth escalating. First, the ICP again has no clinical criterion, and this prospect carries an L3-L4-L5 fusion plus prior clinical advice that his lifting days were over, neither of which any criterion touches. Second, and more usefully: income was the criterion that predicted this outcome exactly, and the call was pursued through four explicit declines anyway. If the ICP is meant to do any screening work, this is the call where it should have stopped things before the price was ever named.
